_provenance.purpose: Hand-curated editorial layer for the /waterways/cooum page. Every fact carries source, date and flag (verified | inferred | asserted). Derived exclusively from docs/research/cooum/ (sections gov-/wq-/hab-/hyd-, per-topic vintages files, data CSVs, primary sources). Banned claims list enforced by scripts/verify_waterway_cooum.py.

reaches.name: The origin: Satharai junction
reaches.verdict: Seasonal channel; fresh flow only by diversion when Poondi reservoir is full

facts.text: The Cooum originates at the junction of the Old Bangaru Channel with the surplus courses of the Cooum and Satharai tanks; WRD gives the river 65 km from here to the sea.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, sections 1.1.3 and 1.2

facts.text: Fresh water enters the river only when Poondi reservoir reaches its full level: 650 cusecs are diverted through Kesavaram anicut for 75 to 90 days, about 51.68 MCM in such a year.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, section 1.7

facts.text: Kesavaram anicut itself stands across the Kosasthalaiyar, not the Cooum; its regulated arm runs about 5 to 7.5 km before it becomes the Cooum - the same DPR calls it the Placis Canal (5 km) in one section and the Old Bangaru Channel (7.5 km) in another. Its construction date is not stated in any primary on our record.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum and Kosasthalaiyar Sub Basin DPRs

facts.text: OpenStreetMap maps no water surface on the first seven kilometres; outside the diversion season the channel here runs dry.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu OSM and Sentinel-2 analysis

reaches.name: Koovam village
reaches.verdict: Tank country past Koovam village; the first mapped water surface

facts.text: The river takes its name from Koovam village in Tiruvallur district, which stands on this stretch with its Tripuranathar temple and temple tank.
facts.source: Madras Musings Vol. XXXII No. 8; Wikimedia Commons records

facts.text: WRD's rain gauges record 712.78 mm a year at Kesavaram anicut and 1,207.97 mm at Korattur anicut.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR

facts.text: Of the sub-basin's 9,937.55 ha of registered tank ayacut, 6,629.52 ha remained available at the DPR; the entire 3,308 ha loss lies in Tiruvallur district, the river's upper country. In Villivakkam block, eleven tanks with 1,376.26 ha of registered ayacut are recorded with present available ayacut nil.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, ayacut tables

reaches.name: The wide bed above Aranvoyal
reaches.verdict: The widest mapped water surface on the river; 86% reads as vegetation from orbit

facts.text: OpenStreetMap maps the river surface here 53 to 321 m wide at the per-km median, the widest mapped water on the river; 2.8 ha of open water shows from orbit this window, and 86% of the mapped surface reads as vegetation.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu OSM transects and Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

facts.text: WRD records the Aranvoyal anicut downstream of this bed 'in fully dilapidated condition' due to illegal sand mining in the river, serviceable only by full reconstruction.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, section 1.1.5

reaches.name: Aranvoyal and Korattur anicuts
reaches.verdict: Open water behind the Aranvoyal and Korattur anicuts; Korattur diverts to Chembarambakkam

facts.text: Aranvoyal anicut (WRD chainage 45.33 km from the mouth) was built to feed Thiruninravur and Gudapakkam tanks; WRD records that the Cooum's two anicuts no longer serve any irrigation command in the sub-basin.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, sections 1.1.5 and 1.7

facts.text: Korattur anicut diverts Cooum water out to Chembarambakkam tank in the Adyar sub-basin through the 7.65 km New Bangaru Canal, maximum capacity 3,627 cusecs; CRRT states the transfer in the present tense.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR; CRRT Cooum River Restoration page

facts.text: Korattur anicut was reported under reconstruction in 2021: Rs 32 crore, NABARD-funded, begun January 2021 and 80% complete by that August, per press reports; no completion statement or government order is on the public record.
facts.source: Press reports, 2021 (no G.O. located)

facts.text: The Krishna water link canal from Poondi to Chembarambakkam crosses the Cooum at Aranvoyal anicut and gathers some of its water on the way.
facts.source: IISc/IIT-M/IIT-B, Chennai Floods 2015: A Rapid Assessment

facts.text: 39.6 ha of open water shows from orbit on this reach this window, the largest on the river; it carries one of the four suspended-sediment readings the river's open water allows.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

reaches.name: The lower pools
reaches.verdict: Pools between the anicuts and the check dam; 16.4 ha of open water this window

facts.text: 15.3 ha of open water and a 52% vegetation share on the mapped water surface this window.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

reaches.name: Paruthipattu check dam
reaches.verdict: Paruthipattu check dam: the eco-restoration project's upstream limit

facts.text: The Paruthipattu check dam is the upstream limit of the Integrated Cooum River Eco-Restoration Project: 'from Paruthipattu check dam to the river mouth in the Bay of Bengal', a stated 32 km.
facts.source: CRRT, Cooum River Restoration page

facts.text: 94.8% of the mapped water surface at the check dam pool reads as vegetation from orbit this window, the highest share on the river.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

facts.text: A PWD environmental-cell sampling point sits downstream of the bridge on the Poonamallee-Avadi road near Paruthipattu.
facts.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, section 1.7 sampling table

reaches.name: Paruthipattu to Poonamallee
reaches.verdict: Desilting and baby-canal formation reported complete (June 2021)

facts.text: PWD's desilting and baby-canal formation on the non-CRZ stretch (chainage 9,677 m to 27,336 m from the mouth) was reported fully complete by June 2021; the baby canal provides a minimum ecological flow path.
facts.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ), progress as on 30.06.2021

facts.text: CPCB's Poonamallee station sits on this reach: 2024 BOD ranged 8-24 mg/L, the lowest of the river's seven stations; mean COD rises station by station downstream, from 93.3 mg/L here to 140.0 near Central Jail.
facts.source: CPCB NWMP, Water Quality of Rivers 2024 (detailed edition)

facts.text: Thirumazhisai Town Panchayat's 3 MLD STP is consented to discharge treated sewage 'into the Cooum River near the Thiruverkadu Minor Canal at the downstream of the Paruthipattu Check Dam' (order renewed 1 July 2026, valid to March 2028).
facts.source: TNPCB OCMMS consent order 62519837

reaches.name: Maduravoyal
reaches.verdict: Maduravoyal: expressway corridor; a 0.6 MLD modular STP in progress (2021)

facts.text: 86% of the mapped water surface on this reach reads as vegetation this window; 246 buildings stand within 50 m of the centerline.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 and Google Open Buildings analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

facts.text: A Rs 17.52 crore diversion channel from Maduravoyal tank to the Cooum (962 cusecs of surplus flood water) was sanctioned in 2009-10; CAG recorded it as not commenced as of January 2017 after the original alignment was built over, with an alternate straight-cut alignment proposed.
facts.source: CAG of India, Report No. 4 of 2017, para 5.1.7

facts.text: In its judgment of 24 March 2026 the NGT directed that WRD's permission to NHAI for the Chennai Port-Maduravoyal Elevated Road Project along the river carry adequate precautionary and flood-mitigation measures, particularly during the monsoon, with GCC and CRRT continuing eco-restoration.
facts.source: NGT (SZ) judgment in O.A. 121 of 2024, 24 Mar 2026

reaches.name: Koyambedu
reaches.verdict: Koyambedu STP cluster: the river's consented treated-sewage inflows

facts.text: The consented discharges into the Cooum are municipal: CMWSSB's 34 MLD and 60 MLD Koyambedu STPs discharge to 'River Coovum', and the 120 MLD plant's remaining treated sewage and the 45 MLD TTRO plant's chain reach the river through a PWD canal. Every one of those orders records trade effluent NIL.

Across 11,583 granted water consents from the five Cooum-corridor TNPCB district offices (2021-2026), fifteen orders name the Cooum as a point of disposal, covering seven facilities, all municipal sewage plants. Nine industrial units near the river hold orders that expressly prohibit discharge of sewage or trade effluent to the Cooum.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu review of the TNPCB OCMMS granted-consent register

facts.text: CMWSSB's underground sewerage scheme at Nerkundram, on this reach's north bank, stood at 32% in June 2021 and 96% in the state's February 2024 status report.
facts.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ); CRRT status report to the NGT, 01.02.2024

reaches.name: Anna Nagar to Aminjikarai
reaches.verdict: The densest built edge on the river: 722 buildings within 50 m

facts.text: 722 buildings stand within 50 m of the centerline on this one reach - more than one in three of the river's total - and 2,963 within 100 m.
facts.source: Google Open Buildings v3 (confidence >= 0.7); Neer Vazhvu proximity analysis

facts.text: Three CPCB stations sit on this reach (Anna Nagar, Arumbakkam, Aminjikarai). The Aminjikarai station's 2021 maximum BOD was 345 mg/L; the 2024 maximum across all seven river stations is 54 mg/L.
facts.source: CPCB NWMP, Water Quality of Rivers 2021 and 2024

facts.text: 17% of the mapped water surface here reads as vegetation this window, against 81 to 86% on the suburban run upstream.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

reaches.name: Chetpet and Nungambakkam
reaches.verdict: Tidal head at Chetpet; two CRRT modular STPs consented to the river

facts.text: PWD gives the river's tidal influencing range as mouth to Chetpet, about 9.4 km; the ICRERP's CRZ-stretch boundary (chainage 9,677 m) lands almost exactly here.
facts.source: CMDA Seminar on Waterways in Chennai (Mar 2010); GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016

facts.text: HSCTC's field survey found this belt holding roughly half its survey-era width: College Bridge to Mc. Nicholas Road measured 99-118 m in the survey records and 47-53 m on the ground in about 2012.
facts.source: HSCTC feasibility report (c. 2012), via the Wikipedia width table of 25 Aug 2013

facts.text: A 1.5 km elevated boardwalk between College Road bridge and Munroe bridge, modelled on the San Antonio River Walk, began work in 2018 under CRRT.
facts.source: Madras Musings Vol. XXXII No. 8

reaches.name: Egmore to the canal junction
reaches.verdict: Egmore to the canal junction: the lowest dissolved-oxygen readings on the river (2024)

facts.text: CPCB's Central Jail station records the river's lowest 2024 readings: dissolved oxygen 0.3 mg/L in every sample, BOD 15-54 mg/L, mean COD 140 mg/L. The 2024 edition publishes no coordinates for this station.
facts.source: CPCB NWMP, Water Quality of Rivers 2024 (detailed edition)

facts.text: The 10 MLD Chintadripet modular STP under CRRT is consented to supply treated water to the railway yard and Corporation avenue plantation - reuse, not the river (orders of 2024 and 2025).
facts.source: TNPCB OCMMS consent orders 59517520, 64956326

facts.text: Eight trash booms were deployed across the city river by June 2021, including near the Buckingham Canal and behind Madras Medical College; the NGT's judgment of 24 March 2026 records the river's compound wall at 20.54 km completed of a total 23.92 km.
facts.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016; NGT (SZ) judgment in O.A. 121 of 2024, 24 Mar 2026

reaches.name: The canal junction and the mouth
reaches.verdict: The canal junction and the engineered mouth

facts.text: The Buckingham Canal crosses the river here (canal chainage km 16.9-19.2, that page's reach 6); the two waterway pages link to each other at this junction.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu waterway geometry (OSM-derived centerlines)

facts.text: WRD's submission to the coastal-zone appraisal records that the river's bed levels near the mouth have fallen below mean sea level and that further desilting would not be useful against the continuously forming sand bar. The works cleared in September 2022 are a pair of curved, NIOT-designed training walls of 265 m and 310 m, with 3,05,000 cubic metres of capital dredging.
facts.source: MoEFCC CRZ clearance F.No.11-25/2022-IA.III, 15 Sep 2022

facts.text: The same clearance mandates a three-year fisheries study and three years of salinity and marine-ecology monitoring at the mouth; no known public copy of either series exists yet.
facts.source: MoEFCC CRZ clearance F.No.11-25/2022-IA.III, conditions

facts.text: WRD's Policy Notes record the Reach-1 mouth works (chainage 0-700 m, revised cost Rs 70 crore) at 95% in 2024-25 and 'all Works have been Completed' in 2025-26; the state's February 2024 status report records the curved training walls under the same package.
facts.source: WRD Policy Notes 2024-25 and 2025-26; CRRT status report to the NGT, 01.02.2024

facts.text: CPCB's Napier Bridge station records conductivity up to 15,820 umho/cm in 2024, against roughly 2,000 at the upstream stations, reflecting the tidal estuary.
facts.source: CPCB NWMP, Water Quality of Rivers 2024

chapters.title: From Satharai to the sea, fifty metres at a time
chapters.verdict: The Cooum runs 62.9 km from its origin near Satharai to the sea at Chennai, measured here end to end, fifty metres at a time. Its fresh water arrives by diversion, its city stretch is tidal, and the state files its water quality to the NGT every month.

chapters.title: Origin and headworks
chapters.verdict: The Cooum rises at the junction of the Old Bangaru Channel with the surplus courses of the Cooum and Satharai tanks. Fresh water enters only when Poondi reservoir reaches its full level, at 650 cusecs for 75 to 90 days (WRD), and the upstream tanks' available irrigation command has fallen from 9,938 ha registered to 6,630 ha.

chapters.title: The anicuts
chapters.verdict: Between km 17.5 and 31 the river holds its only upstream open water, behind the Aranvoyal and Korattur anicuts and the Paruthipattu check dam. WRD records Aranvoyal as not serviceable after sand mining; Korattur diverts Cooum water to Chembarambakkam through the New Bangaru Canal; the check dam is the upstream limit of the Integrated Cooum River Eco-Restoration Project.

chapters.title: Paruthipattu to Koyambedu
chapters.verdict: From Paruthipattu to Koyambedu, 81 to 86% of the mapped water surface reads as vegetation in the Jun-Aug 2026 Sentinel-2 window. At Koyambedu the consented inflows begin: CMWSSB's treated sewage, with trade effluent recorded NIL on every order that names the river. No industrial consent names the Cooum as a point of disposal.

chapters.title: The monitoring record
chapters.verdict: The state files Cooum water quality monthly to the NGT: BOD 13-24 mg/L across seven locations in May 2026, against the bathing-water standard of 3 mg/L. The CPCB annual series runs to 2024; the TNPCB CCWW report's last published edition covers 2022-23.

chapters.title: The city channel
chapters.verdict: The HSCTC field survey (c. 2012) measured the city stretches at roughly a third to a half of their survey-era widths. The state's February 2024 status report records eleven of thirteen interception packages complete, the Langs Garden treatment plant at 97% and the Nerkundram sewerage scheme at 96%.

chapters.title: Encroachment and resettlement
chapters.verdict: TNSCB's December 2015 enumeration recorded encroachment on 22.7 of 80 bank-kilometres, with 14,257 project-affected families; 13,056 had been resettled by mid-2022 (Madras High Court record) and 13,484, with 773 remaining, by the state's February 2024 filing - a figure TNUHDB's policy notes repeat unchanged through 2025-26. In July 2025 the Madras High Court recorded that the government wants to restore the river and that the project remains struck on account of the remaining encroachments; in February 2026 the Supreme Court directed a joint Revenue-PWD inspection with notice and objections within four months, with status quo on demolition and construction meanwhile.

chapters.title: The river mouth
chapters.verdict: PWD's record lists twelve schemes for keeping the mouth open between 1890 and 2000. The current works, cleared in September 2022, are NIOT-designed training walls with a mandated three-year fisheries and salinity study; WRD's Policy Notes record the Reach-1 mouth works 95% complete (2024-25) and completed (2025-26).

chapters.title: The restoration programme
chapters.verdict: The current administrative sanction is Rs 735.08 crore, with Rs 604.75 crore disbursed (MAWS Policy Note 2025-26). The 2024-25 note stated completion by October 2024 except remaining resettlement; the 2025-26 note states all restoration works are expected to be completed soon. The 2026-27 revised budget announced global tenders and a new DPR for the Cooum and the Adyar. On CRRT's Adyar creek restoration, the department reports a faunal count of about 424 species against 141 before restoration.

silt_ledger.text: WRD's submission to the coastal-zone appraisal: the river's bed levels near the mouth have already fallen below mean sea level, and further desilting there would not be useful because of the continuous formation of the sand bar.
silt_ledger.source: MoEFCC CRZ clearance F.No.11-25/2022-IA.III, recording WRD

silt_ledger.text: Sand deposition at the mouth, assessed at 1,75,000 cubic metres a year, is designed to fall to 8,000 cubic metres a year (4.57%) once the training walls are built; 3,05,000 cubic metres of capital dredging was cleared with them.

The mouth works carry a Rs 70.00 crore administrative sanction for continuous opening and desilting from the mouth to Napier Bridge (G.O.(Ms) No.76, MAWS (MC-I), 31 July 2020), with the design tested on a physical model at IHH Poondi.
silt_ledger.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ), as on 30.06.2021

silt_ledger.text: The mouth works' recorded progression: curved training walls under progress in the state's status report of 1 February 2024; 95% complete in WRD's Policy Note 2024-25; 'all Works have been Completed' in the 2025-26 note.
silt_ledger.source: CRRT status report to the NGT (01.02.2024); WRD Policy Notes 2024-25 and 2025-26

silt_ledger.text: PWD's own record lists twelve schemes for sustained opening of the mouth between 1890 and 2000, from staged groynes to a 400 m tidal weir proposed at Napier Bridge in 1922.
silt_ledger.source: CMDA Seminar on Waterways in Chennai, Session III

width_ledger.note: The city river, bridge by bridge. 'Recorded in the survey era' is the river's width in the original survey records, the full recorded extent including banks. 'Found in ~2012' is what the HSCTC feasibility study measured on the ground. In every column the two numbers are the minimum and maximum along that stretch. In the table, the mouth-to-Napier Bridge stretch is the only one whose measured width equals its survey width.
width_ledger.source: HSCTC (Chennai High Speed Circular Transportation Corridors) feasibility report, c. 2012, via Wikipedia (table added 25 Aug 2013)

methods.title: Length and chainage
methods.body: The 62.9 km alignment is chained from OpenStreetMap's river geometry (ODbL, snapshot August 2026): the Cooum is mapped as a single continuous way from the origin junction near Satharai to the mouth, resampled every 50 m. WRD's own DPR gives the river 65 km from the same origin; the difference is tracing generalisation. Whole-length uncertainty: about plus or minus 1-2%.

methods.title: Widths (the 1,258 transects)
methods.body: Every 50 m of chainage we cast a perpendicular line and measure the water-surface polygon traced by OpenStreetMap contributors (most edits 2021-2026). 1,049 transects return a measurement; the first seven kilometres have no mapped water surface (a rural, seasonal channel) and read unmeasured by design. 50 m sampling sits at the resolution of the source itself: the traced bank lines place a vertex every 22 m at the median, so sampling much finer would only re-read straight drawn edges. Width here is water surface at the tracing moment, not the river's recorded (poramboke) land. Each reach carries a confidence tier: A = at least 70% measured, tracing mostly 2021 or later, and width jitter at 200 m separation of 25% or less; B = measured but sparse or older tracing; C = not channel-measurable. Jitter is always evaluated at about 200 m separation, whatever the sampling density, so denser sampling cannot inflate a tier.

methods.title: Satellite metrics (Sentinel-2, 10 m pixels)
methods.body: Cloud-masked median composites: January-April and June-August 2026. Vegetation = NDVI above 0.35; open water = NDWI above 0. Vegetation on the water is computed strictly inside the mapped water polygons (floating plus emergent growth); corridor figures also include about 8 m of bank each side and read higher. The condition strip reads a 25 m disc every 50 m of chainage; with 10 m pixels, 50 m is the honest floor for this - finer bins would re-count the same pixels. Threshold choice moves fractions by roughly 5-10 percentage points; 10 m pixels undercount water in channels narrower than about 30 m. The suspended-sediment reading (NDTI) is a relative index over open water, not a mg/L measurement. Site images are clearest-pixel composites; segment images are medians; each is dated on the image.

methods.title: The built edge
methods.body: Google Open Buildings v3 footprints (2023 release, confidence at least 0.7) counted within 50 m and 100 m of the centerline. Deliberately conservative: measured from the centerline, not the river's recorded boundary; the confidence filter trims small structures; three years of construction post-date the data. A 'none mapped' reads exactly that: nothing in the dataset, not proof of nothing on the ground.

methods.title: Estimated widths (why this page ships none)
methods.body: The canal page fills its OSM-blind transects with labelled spectral estimates; this page deliberately does not. The Cooum's unmeasured stretch (the first seven kilometres) runs dry outside the diversion season - the estimator found water on only 9 of 203 blind transects - and its calibration against this river's OSM-measured transects failed our quality gate (water detected on 62 of 150; median disagreement 37.4 m, driven by weed-covered surfaces the near-infrared test reads as land). An estimate that calibrates this poorly would be a number without meaning, so the dots stay dots. The build applies this gate mechanically: estimates ship only where detection reaches half the measured transects and agreement is within 20 m.

methods.title: Check the numbers yourself
methods.body: Every input is public: OpenStreetMap (ODbL, snapshot date stated), Copernicus Sentinel-2, Google Open Buildings, and the cited government documents - many held as local primary copies (the WRD Cooum sub-basin DPR, the MAWS and WRD Policy Notes, NGT filings, TNPCB consent orders, CPCB monitoring PDFs, the CRZ clearance). Every derived number on this page is recomputed independently from the raw inputs before publication by a published audit script (scripts/audit_waterway_numbers_cooum.py in the Neer Vazhvu repository), and the claim register (claims.json) carries a per-number citation a reader can pull and compare.

methods.title: What this page deliberately does not compute
methods.body: Depth, silt volume and flow: no satellite can measure them in water this narrow and turbid, the river has no known public flow gauge, and we would rather show a gap than an estimate without an instrument. They are the first work of the measurement layer this page proposes: level and flow gauging, a boat-run depth survey, and field checks under the vegetation the satellite flags.
